newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FORECAST-Brazil trade gap $7 bln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Brazil trade gap $7 bln in 1997.

text.p: An economic think-tank said the trade deficit will rise to $7 billion in 1997 compared with an estimated $5 billion gap in 1996, local television reported.

TV Globo, quoting a report by the Rio de Janeiro-based Getulio Vargas Foundation's Brazilian Economic Institute (Ibre), said the trade deficit swelled in 1996 due to the slow growth of exports compared with quickly rising imports.
The Ibre report said imports rose 3.3 percent while exports moved up only a slight 0.4 percent last year, Globo said.
The growing trade gap, which reached $3.15 billion in 1995, has sparked market speculation that the government may speed up devaluation of the real currency to boost exports.
The Ibre also said direct foreign investment in Brazil reached a record $9 billion in 1996, up 174 percent from the prior year.
